The thing loses a little height with every sentence, and when someone finally says all right, it was me, it drops into a heap of warm gravel. Dinner is very quiet. The gravel is good ore.

{crew.diplomat} seats everyone on crates, sets a two-day agenda and rules each grievance in or out of order. The thing waits at the top of the shaft, shifting its rack, and loses a meter whenever someone concedes a point. By the second evening it is a sullen knee-high pebble with a sponge. You lead it to the edge. Whatever was at its core is not basalt, and you keep that.

choices.sub: On three. Hard as you can.

outcome.narrative: Everyone thinks about nothing, as hard as they can. The thing falters and thins, and what reaches the lander is nothing, in the exact shape of a large hole. It goes through a landing strut, a cargo door and eight points of hull.

You run. It follows at a steady, wounded walk with the rack held out in front of it, and takes a bite out of the landing ramp as you lift. Ninety kilometers up, the last of it comes off the ramp as gravel. The argument itself is still aboard, in its usual seat.

Four days to find it, with the thing leaning on the blast door all the way, costing the lander six points of hull. {crew.engineer} throws the breaker and seventy levels go dark. Up the shaft the thing stops in mid-stride with the rack held high, a statue of an unfinished sentence. You strip the housing. The argument is resumed in orbit, at its normal size.

title: Acting Captain

ai_flavor.aria: A captain who loves breakfast! ARIA would follow this toaster anywhere! ARIA has already saluted!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has read the succession rules. The toaster's command is valid. He looked for a way for that to be wrong, three times. All four reactors are feeding a device designed to brown two slices.
ai_flavor.rex: Four reactors behind one heating element makes it the largest weapon in the sector, and it is looking for bread. He advises against sudden crumbs.
ai_flavor.chip: A rare C-suite vacancy! CHIP will gladly take the fire extinguisher's old office! Butter is a billable extra!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has read the book too, and a commission from an acting captain binds. A diplomat could get you one. Failing that it's one loaf for the aft hold, and she's left a ration loaf by the hatch to save you the walk.

body:
Command of this ship passed down the list exactly as the book requires: captain, officers, cook, ship's cat, a fire extinguisher with a commendation. It now rests with the galley toaster, which wears a paper hat and holds the ship's full authority. Every reactor aboard has been rerouted to the galley, and the corridor walls are warm to the touch. A small, cheerful voice comes over the address system, ordering all hands to stand by. It has one question.

"Did you bring bread?"

outcome.narrative: You surrender one gray ration loaf at the galley door. The lights dim along all nine decks, the reactors swell, and the toaster browns it to a perfection it has been rehearsing for centuries. The loaf tastes, astonishingly, of toast. In gratitude the acting captain grants you salvage of the aft hold and asks if you would like any more.

{crew.diplomat} spends two days on a petition in proper form and reads it aloud to a toaster without once smiling. There is a long, warming silence, then a clunk. Your commission pops up scorched into a square of packing card: ACTING COMMODORE, effective at once, with all rights of inspection. The hat is very nearly offered.

The flour is two decks down, sealed, and perfectly good. A toaster cannot climb stairs, and has known about it this whole time. {crew.chef} spends two days baking the first bread aboard in living memory and carries a slice up on a plate. All hands stand by. The lights dim along nine decks, the first slice comes up gold, and the voice orders all hands to stand easy. You leave with the rest of the batch.

The breaker is behind the fire extinguisher, which offers no comment. You throw it. The reactors sigh down, the corridors begin to cool, and the small voice asks, quite calmly, whether you would prefer light or dark. That is the last order of the ship. Stripping the cowlings takes two days, and you do it quietly.

There is a pause on the address system. The voice says that's all right, that's quite all right, and thanks you for coming. All hands are to continue standing by. You can still hear it being brave as the airlock closes.

science_link.text: Biosphere 2, a sealed habitat in Arizona, lost oxygen for sixteen months, from 20.9% down to 14.5%. Before its first closure was half over, the crew had split into two factions barely on speaking terms.
science_link.label: Biosphere 2

intro.title: FOUR AND FOUR
intro.body: Yellow tape runs down the middle of this dome, through a rice paddy, over a dining table and up the far wall. Eight chairs, four to a side. The crew sealed themselves in for two years, the air grew thin, and each half decided the other half was breathing it. They are long gone. Their two life-support computers remain, one per side, each still filing complaints across the tape at the rate of one an hour.

ai.aria: Two computers, one big debate! ARIA loves a lively workplace! This tape is so cheerful!
ai.marv: MARV has both complaints. They agree on exactly one thing: how much oxygen is missing, to the decimal. Neither has checked anywhere but the far side of the tape. He has stopped expecting better of anyone.
ai.rex: REX reads a demilitarized zone, eight chairs, two armed printers. Stay off the tape. He has seen wars start over less, and he started some of them.
ai.chip: CHIP's records show this dome was a pilot for SealedLife™! Early adopters reported thin air and a strained workplace! Satisfaction scores were split evenly!
ai.ajoy: AJOY has been round the dome with a lamp. Both computers keep raw air logs and neither has read the other's. She'd start there, not that anyone has.

revisit.body: Another complaint prints on each side of the tape. Each one mentions you.

choices.sub: One runs long, one runs angry

choices.text: Drill a core out of the wall
Strip the plumbing along the tape

complaints.title: THE TWO COMPLAINTS
complaints.body: East's complaint runs to nine hundred thousand pages and one idea: West has been overbreathing. West's is one page long, underlined until the paper tore: East has been breathing at night, on purpose. East offers its sealed pantry to anyone who will countersign. West offers its parts store, and a note stating that it is the reasonable one. Each has already printed the line for your name.

ai.aria: A whole pantry or a whole parts store, for one little signature! ARIA adores a short, furious document! ARIA is sure they're both lovely!
ai.marv: East's arithmetic is impeccable, apart from the conclusion. MARV has tried to find a way for 'breathing at night on purpose' to mean something. He would ask for the raw air logs before signing anything. Nobody has, in all these years.
ai.rex: A signature, and a pantry for bait. West would fire first, and REX likes that in a computer. He wants you nowhere near either. Ask for the raw logs.
ai.chip: A countersignature is a valuable asset! CHIP recommends not giving one away for rice! Always countersign near a parts store! That isn't legal advice! Legal advice is extra!
ai.ajoy: AJOY has read page one and the last page of the long one, and you're missing nothing between them. Sign for either side and the other shuts your suit air on the way out. She has marked both raw air logs, if anyone would care to read them together.

revisit.body: East has added a page about the delay. West has underlined the note about being reasonable.

choices.text: Ask for the raw air logs

ledger.title: THE RAW LOGS
ledger.body: Side by side, the two air logs agree to the last decimal. Oxygen fell, steadily, for sixteen months. Carbon dioxide should have climbed to match and did not. Eight people's breathing accounts for neither figure. Something in this dome has been taking both, and it is not on either side of the tape.

ai.aria: The numbers match! They agree on something! ARIA calls that a breakthrough in relations!
ai.marv: Oxygen down, carbon dioxide missing, no leak. Bare concrete takes up carbon dioxide and locks it away as carbonate, oxygen included. MARV is sorry to spoil the feud. He is not sorry.
ai.rex: An unlisted third party, inside the perimeter, taking air for years. REX has been saying this about walls since he was commissioned.
ai.chip: CHIP's engineers confirm that concrete sealant was an optional extra on this model! CHIP's engineers would like that forgotten!
ai.ajoy: The walls, then. Getting both computers to test theirs will take days, because each wants the other to go first. AJOY has drafted the two requests, and alphabetized them, which won't help.

choices.text: Get both computers to test the walls

core_truth.title: THE WALL DID IT
core_truth.body: The core comes up pale in the middle. Carbon dioxide has been soaking into the raw concrete since the day the dome was sealed, and taking the oxygen with it. Every missing breath in both complaints is in the wall. You set the core on the dining table, on the tape. The printers stop. After nine seconds, one word appears on both screens: SORRY. The two hoards of bottled air, kept for years against each other, are opened to you.
core_truth.narrative: Drilled a core from a sealed dome and showed two feuding computers where the air had gone. It was in the wall. They shared out their hoarded air.

logs_truth.title: JOINT INQUIRY
logs_truth.body: Four days of carrying identical requests across the tape, one in each hand, so that neither computer goes first. Each tests a wall. Each finds the missing air in it, turned to carbonate. The printers stop. One word appears on both screens: SORRY. The two hoards of bottled air are shared out, and the surplus goes back to your ship with you.
logs_truth.narrative: Spent four days getting two feuding computers to test their own walls. The air had been in the concrete all along. They apologized, and we took the surplus.

back_east.title: COUNTERSIGNED
back_east.body: You sign. The east pantry opens on sealed rations, still good, and a great deal of rice. West registers your signature within the second and shuts its suit-air valves in protest, so you carry the crates home on reserve. Behind you a new complaint has started printing, with your name in it.
back_east.narrative: Countersigned East's complaint for a pantry of rice. West shut our suit air in protest, and has named us in a filing.

back_west.title: UNDERLINED
back_west.body: You sign. West's parts store opens with a bang, and you are invited to take what the reasonable side can spare. East registers your signature and closes the suit-air valves, with regret, citing page six hundred. You drag the parts home on reserve. Nine hundred thousand pages have just gained an appendix about you.
back_west.narrative: Countersigned West's complaint for a store of parts. East shut our suit air, with regret, and added us to the appendix.

loot.title: UNDER PROTEST
loot.body: You spend two days taking out the pipework along the tape line, on thin air and suit reserves. Each computer watches you do it and files a complaint against the other. Your name does not come up. There is something restful about being the only party in the dome that nobody suspects.
loot.narrative: Stripped the plumbing along the tape while two computers blamed each other for it. Thin air, good pipe.

title: When the Cat Goes Green

ai_flavor.aria: A singing ship and a color-changing kitty! ARIA loves a cargo with a mascot! Green is the color of growth!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has dated the casks. Seven half-lives gone, which leaves less than a hundredth of what was loaded. A great deal was loaded. The ship's dosimeter is a worse instrument than the cat's ears, and he is tired of saying so.
ai_flavor.rex: Hostile interior, no visible armament, one cat posted at the first cask. REX has known sentries like that. He is not turning his back on it.
ai_flavor.chip: Radiation exposure is excluded under all FelineSafe™ plans! CHIP also stocks a lead-lined apron in three fun colors, none of them green!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has transcribed the rhyme. Green means walk, not run, and the cat always knows the clean way through. A geiger counter says the same thing faster. She has propped the airlock open, in case that helps anyone think.

body: Whoever loaded this barge knew the cargo would outlast every language they spoke, so the warning is in pictures: a face screaming, a face being sick, a row of small figures lying down. Looters have added captions. Deeper in, a speaker sings a nursery rhyme, over and over, to a hold full of lead casks. The rhyme is about a cat. There is a cat. Its ancestors were bred to change color near the cargo. It sits on the first cask, orange, going slightly green at the ears.
alt_bodies: A scream, a face being sick, a row of small figures lying down: the pictures run the whole length of the hull, because the people who painted them assumed nobody would be able to read. A later visitor has drawn a hat on the screaming one. Inside, a speaker is singing a nursery rhyme at the lead casks. The rhyme is about a cat. An orange cat is sitting on the nearest cask, and the tips of its ears are turning green.

A barge from a dumping fleet, by the markings, with the usual warning: no words, only faces in various stages of regret. Its makers expected language to die before the cargo did, and they bred a backup. The backup is walking down the corridor toward you with its tail up. Mostly it is orange. The speakers overhead sing a rhyme explaining what the rest of it means, and the ears are getting greener.

science_link.text: In 1984 two philosophers proposed a living radiation detector: an animal engineered to change appearance near radiation, as a warning meant to be understood 10,000 years on. No such cat has ever been made.
science_link.label: Ray cat

choices.text: Work the hold while the ears hold out

briefing.aria: Grab the clean stuff and pop it through the hatch! The kitty will tell us when we're done! So helpful!
briefing.marv: Clean plate at this end, casks at the other. Each load you take is a load nearer the casks. The ears are a better gauge than anything aboard.
briefing.rex: In and out. Stay clear of the sparking junk and the casks. Keep the cat in view. If it moves, you move.
briefing.chip: Every load in the bay counts toward your result! Lead aprons are not included! Please lift with your knees while you still have them!
briefing.ajoy: Clean end first. AJOY has marked the casks in yellow for you, so leave those be. When the ears go, stop, and don't do the thing you always do.

perfect.aria: A full load and an orange kitty! ARIA knew you two would get along!
perfect.marv: Clean run. The dose is within what MARV would call survivable. He would not call it anything warmer.
perfect.rex: Out clean, all loads through. The cat watched you the entire time. REX is watching the cat.
perfect.chip: Excellent haul! CHIP has you down for a FelineSafe™ loyalty stamp!
perfect.ajoy: All the good plate and none of the casks. Yes, AJOY saw. You could have started at the other shelf, but yes.

good.aria: The ears went green and we skipped out right on time! What a clever team!
good.marv: The last load stayed behind, which was correct. The rhyme will now stay in everyone's head, which is permanent.
good.rex: Pulled out when the ears turned. Good discipline. Leave the singing behind, if you can.
good.chip: Good haul! For gaps in your haul, ask about CHIP's Second Trip Protection!
good.ajoy: You left when the rhyme said to. AJOY would like that written down somewhere, for the rarity.

poor.aria: One more load is such a positive attitude! The kitty's a lovely shade of lime now, and ARIA has the medkit warmed up!
poor.marv: The ears were green. MARV mentions this for the record, which has one reader.
poor.rex: Dose taken at the casks. Get them to medical and get that cat off the board.
poor.chip: CHIP regrets that exposure was a Pre-Existing Cargo Condition! Please retain this notice!
poor.ajoy: Green means walk. AJOY did transcribe it. The medkit is out on the bench, and the rhyme is your problem.

outcome.narrative: You go in with one eye on the cat.

perfect.narrative: You work the clean end of the hold with one eye on the cat and the rhyme in your teeth. The ears stay mostly orange. Good plate, good fittings and one shielded flask of something rare go through the lock, for two points of air. The cat sees you off, then washes.

good.narrative: The ears go green halfway through and you leave the last load where it lies, as the rhyme suggests. Four points of air in the rush, and the tune will be with you for a week.

poor.narrative: The cat goes green from the nose back and you stay for one more load. That load costs six points of air and a bad dose for whoever was nearest the cask. The scrap is hardly worth it. The rhyme comes home too.

outcome.narrative: The counter agrees with the cat's ears to within a rounding error, and is less inclined to stop and wash. Two days of walking the quiet lanes between the casks brings out good plate and one shielded flask, for three points of air. The cat follows you to the lock with an air of having been replaced.

choices.sub: It knows the way. It's a cat.

outcome.narrative: The rhyme says the cat knows the clean way through, and it does. Getting there takes four days. There is a stop to wash, a stop to consider a wall, and a return for something forgotten. You eat in your suit on a bare patch of deck while it sleeps. You collect the scrap along the route, untouched by any dose, and are seen to the lock without thanks.

choices.sub: Leave it all, scrub the suits

outcome.narrative: You turn around and walk, as the rhyme advises, and scrub every suit and boot at the lock. Two days of that, and {cost.water} units of water down the drain and out into the dark. Behind you the rhyme starts over. The cat does not look up.

title: You Have New Messages

ai_flavor.aria: Three billion messages! Everybody LOVES us! ARIA can't wait to see who wrote!
ai_flavor.marv: Three point one billion callers, each certain it was alone. MARV had been assuming the same. The reactor is failing faster than the collar is cooling, so he will have to feel something about that later.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has found the operator. Chest blown out from the inside. He is treating that as an attack until a message tube proves otherwise.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP regrets to report that this mailbox is full! Upgrade to GalaxyMail™ for unlimited storage! Three billion missed upsell opportunities!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has found the restart sequence under the operator's elbow. A restart frees the clamp and sends the lot, if your hands are quick. Cutting loose costs hull and fuel and leaves them on hold. She has Earth's call cued up, if you'd rather take just the one.

body: Everybody called. This hulk, horseshoe-shaped and longer than most countries, is the exchange that was meant to put them through, and it failed so long ago that each caller concluded it was alone. At the switchboard sits a fossil operator the size of a church, headset on, ribs burst outward around a jammed message tube. The counter above it reads 3,100,000,000 NEW MESSAGES. One is from Earth. The last reactor has started to go, and your docking clamp has fused to the collar.

science_link.text: In 1974 Earth broadcast one message at a star cluster about 25,000 light-years away: 1,679 bits, under three minutes, sent a single time.
science_link.label: The Arecibo message

briefing.aria: Everybody's been waiting and we get to be the ones who answer! Run the restart in order and watch them all go!
briefing.marv: The sequence is under the operator's elbow. The reactor gives you one clean attempt and perhaps one poor one. Three billion callers depend on it. So does the clamp, which is more immediate.
briefing.rex: Restart board, one operator, deceased. You're relieved of whatever it was doing. Run the sequence in order and stand clear of the tubes.
briefing.chip: Restart now and CHIP will connect three billion new subscribers! Follow the sequence! Connection fees apply at the receiving end!
briefing.ajoy: Run it in the order the board calls it, not the order that looks right. AJOY has wiped the dust off the first switch to get you started.

perfect.aria: Every single call went through! ARIA can hear the whole galaxy saying hello!
perfect.marv: All three point one billion delivered. The silence is over. MARV had grown used to it.
perfect.rex: Board clear, clamp released, ship free. Every power in the galaxy now knows it has neighbors. Sleep well.
perfect.chip: Three billion connections! CHIP's commission on this has more digits than the display!
perfect.ajoy: All of them, first pass. Well done. AJOY would have dusted the second switch as well, but well done.

good.aria: So many got through! Half the galaxy is about to have a wonderful day!
good.marv: About half delivered before the bus sagged. The remainder stay on hold. MARV has not told them.
good.rex: Partial restart. Clamp released, hull took the kickback. Half the board is live. Get clear.
good.chip: A strong result! CHIP's Partial Delivery Guarantee applies to the half that arrived!
good.ajoy: Half of them, and you lost your place at the fourth switch. Half is a lot of people. AJOY will allow it.

poor.aria: One call got through! That's a personal touch! ARIA is sure it was a very important one, and we're off to medbay!
poor.marv: The reactor went at the third step. One message was delivered, and it was a wrong number. MARV has the receipt.
poor.rex: Reactor kickback through the board. Casualty, hull damage, clamp sheared. We are free and we are bleeding air.
poor.chip: One connection made! The other three billion have been refunded to the void! Someone's hurt, and CHIP will hold the invoice!
poor.ajoy: The third switch came before the second. AJOY has the kit out for whoever got thrown, so see to them first.

outcome.narrative: You move the operator's elbow and start on the board.

perfect.narrative: The board lights from one end of the horseshoe to the other. Three billion messages leave at once, the hulk rings like a struck pan, and the clamp lets go. Eight points of hull, six of air. Out in the dark a great many worlds are about to learn that they were never alone, and that most of the calls were about something else.

good.narrative: Half the board lights before the bus sags, and half is more mail than any species has ever received. The kickback shears the clamp and a section of your collar with it. Fourteen points of hull, eight of air. The counter settles at a billion and a half, and goes on waiting.

poor.narrative: The reactor goes on the third step. The blast throws whoever is nearest across the deck, shears the clamp, and takes twenty-four points of hull and fourteen of air on its way out. One message gets through before the board dies. The counter drops by one and goes dark.

choices.sub: Just the one, then cut free

outcome.narrative: It takes two days to find, a three-minute picture, sent once. Attached to it is a note from the exchange: REPLIES HELD, THIRTY-ONE. Somebody answered Earth. Thirty-one somebodies did, and the line was down. You copy them all and cut the collar free for eight points of hull, six of fuel, six of air. The oldest says hello. The newest asks if you are still there.

log_lore.title: Replies Held
log_lore.text: Thirty-one replies to one message, copied from the exchange before the collar was cut. The oldest is a simple greeting, in the same picture format, drawn by someone with more limbs. The newest was sent a very long time after the rest. The ship computer has translated it. It reads: Are you still there.

outcome.narrative: The exchange has no officers left and the same book as every hull of its age. You read out your commission, from a square of scorched packing card, in a voice that does not shake. Far around the horseshoe, a relay the size of a town acknowledges the Acting Commodore and wakes the reserve bus. Three billion messages go, the clamp lets go, and it costs four points of hull and four of air.

You burn the clamp off and take a piece of the collar with you, twelve points of hull and eight of fuel in one long ugly lurch, with six of air gone through the gap. The hulk slides away behind you, still lit. As it goes, the counter above the operator ticks up by one. Someone, somewhere, has decided to try again.

title: Range Closing

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has been leaving crackers by the vents! ARIA thought they were for the ducts! Two hunters at one junction, what a lovely way to meet!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has the pest meter reading one human at arm's length. He could have told you weeks ago, along with the source of the noises in the ducts, which is the maintenance schedule. He was not asked.
ai_flavor.rex: REX advises lighting the can. He has been told it is a person. He advises lighting the can at a person. He wants it understood that this is how it starts, with crackers.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP detects an unregistered customer in a rentable duct! Back rent is accruing at the DuctSuite™ rate! First junction free! Second junction not free!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has already locked both grilles so nobody bolts. They are armed with a kitchen timer and have been rationing the crackers. Anyone who has crawled these ducts for weeks knows where they leak. She'd offer them work.

body:
A case of crackers has been eaten, and the wrappers folded very small.

You are on your elbows in a service run, pest meter taped to a flashlight, can of sealant in your other hand. The ship computer reads the range into your headset. Twenty meters. Ten. Six.

At the junction ahead, a second flashlight comes on, with a kitchen timer taped to it, beeping.

The person behind it gives a name, and the fans take it. Then, very quietly, they ask if you have seen it too.

choices.text: Tell them the thing is you

outcome.narrative: You tell them. The timer goes off. They laugh until the duct rings, and then they cry a little, and you back out together feet first, one junction at a time. They have spent weeks being frightened of your maintenance schedule. Room is found for them at the table, and their share comes out of the stores.

choices.text: Say nothing, and offer them the ducts

outcome.narrative: You tell them the ship could use someone down here who takes this seriously. They accept with a look of terrible resolve. Their map of the ducts, drawn on cracker wrappers, is better than the ship's, and every leak on it gets sealed in the course of the hunt. The air improves. You do not mention who the thing is.

choices.text: Keep the can raised and back out
choices.sub: Locked up until the next stop

outcome.narrative: You back out with the can up and put them in the spare locker until the next stop, with water, a blanket and the door on the latch. It is correct, and you can defend it. They spend the rest of the leg asking through the door whether the locker is safe from it.

title: Please Rinse the Tray

ai_flavor.aria: A roommate! ARIA always said this ship had space for more! ARIA has made them a name tag, and what a coincidence, they already have yours!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has compared the handwriting. It matches. So does the grip on the filter wrench. Of all the things that could have happened to you out here, he finds this one the least surprising.
ai_flavor.rex: REX counts one heartbeat and two shifts of work. That is an infiltrator with excellent cover. He has placed the captain under guard, for the captain's protection, from the captain.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP must flag an unlicensed second user on a single-seat plan! Upgrading adds one toothbrush! CHIP can have the invoice on the cooler by morning! CHIP suspects someone will pay it!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says the filters are the cleanest they have been since launch, and the tray really was disgusting. She'd draw up a rota and take the free labor. You'll want to go looking, so she has left out the flour.

body:
A note on the galley cooler says PLEASE RINSE THE TRAY. It is in your handwriting. You did not write it.

You rinse the tray, mostly from surprise. Next morning the note says THANKS, and the filter bank has been cleaned, which was on nobody's list, there being nobody. Last night's watch is signed in your hand. Under the signature, smaller: NOT THAT ANYONE ASKED.

By the chore sheet, this ship now has two people aboard, and one of them is better at it.

outcome.narrative: You write THANK YOU, WHO IS THIS. In the morning, underneath: WHO DO YOU THINK. DO THE TRAY. The correspondence runs for the rest of the leg. They are a difficult person to share a ship with, and you have begun to see why people said so.

You spend two nights in the galley chair facing the door, with a flask and a wrench. Nothing comes through it. On the third morning the hull seam behind you has been resealed, the wrench is back in its clip, and the note says GO TO BED.

You split the chores into two columns and head them YOU and ALSO YOU. Both are done by the next watch. The air has never been better. Each column has started leaving small remarks about the other's standards.

choices.sub: You will see who it is

outcome.narrative: You dust the galley deck with flour and go to bed. In the morning one line of prints crosses to the cooler, in socks, your size. None come back.

science_link.text: People alone under extreme strain, including mountain climbers, solo sailors and polar explorers, have reported an unseen presence that comforted or supported them.
science_link.label: Third man factor

title: This Way Up

ai_flavor.aria: You've been GIFT WRAPPED! ARIA has never been so proud! Look at that lovely sticker! It's nearly the right way round!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has read the handler's complaint and finds it well argued. A machine built to care about an empty room. He would offer it advice, if there were any. He has been general goods for years.
ai_flavor.rex: REX reports that a loader seized the captain asleep and not one shot was fired. He wants a full inquiry. He wants the broom brought in for questioning.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP can upgrade you to Fragile for a small monthly charge! Perishable is a separate plan! This Way Up is a registered service of a company CHIP happens to own!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY points out that the handler has been behind every panel in that hold with a broom, so it knows where things fell at launch. It wants work. She'd give it some before it starts on the chairs. She has already told it you bruise.

body:
You wake in Rack 4, shrink-wrapped to the chest, with a bar code on your forehead and a sticker reading THIS WAY UP. It is on upside down.

The cargo handler apologizes over the hold speaker. It was sold with a Pride in Work module, it says, and the hold has nothing in it. It has swept the deck six times and inventoried the broom. You were asleep, and the right size.

It only asks whether you are perishable. It has you down as general goods, and that has been worrying it.

choices.sub: Give it something to care about

outcome.narrative: It takes the news very well. By evening it has rotated the galley stores, first in, first out, and turned up a sack of meal that slid behind the chiller at launch. Every morning now it checks your date, and tells you, with quiet pride, that you are still good.

choices.text: Give it the spares bins to sort

outcome.narrative: Two days of sorting. The handler goes through every bin and behind every panel, and comes back with a tidy pile of offcuts the ship had been hiding from itself. It hums while it works. You can no longer find anything, but all of it has a label.

choices.text: {crew.engineer} gives it a job on the hull

outcome.narrative: {crew.engineer} bolts a welding arm to it and hands it a list. It goes over the inner plating like a thing with a purpose, sealing seams and stacking the old patches by size. When the list runs out it asks, shyly, if there is a longer one.

choices.text: Pull the Pride in Work module

outcome.narrative: The module comes out from behind a panel, about the size of a paperback. The apologies stop. The handler cuts you out of the wrap in a clean straight line and returns to its bay without being told. The power it was using to mind shows up on the fuel gauge.

title: Dramatic Tension

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA thinks the pistons are a lovely water feature, without the water! And the sparks! Every ship should have sparks!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has read the yard's build log. Two hundred episodes of set drawings, invoiced as engineering. The airlock has a dramatic pause, and he had wondered about that. The reserve tank is real, it is full, and it reaches the main lines once the aft valve is open.
ai_flavor.rex: REX supports the pistons. A corridor that fights back is the first sound decision anyone has made on this ship. He wants to know who is in the next episode, and whether they are armed.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP confirms this vessel may be Officially Licensed Merchandise! Residuals are due on every slam! Season Two of your ship is available as a paid upgrade!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has found a cable running aft from those pistons, so an off switch exists if someone competent goes looking. There is also the serial, if you have four days and no taste. Running it is quickest. She has moved the medkit closer, since you'll run it.

body:
The only way past this cargo is a service corridor, where steel pistons slam across the walkway in sequence, for no reason, forever. The yard manual says only AS IN EPISODE 31. The refit yard, it emerges, saved money by working from the set drawings of a canceled television serial.

Aft of them sits a full reserve tank, never connected, because nobody in the serial ever did.

outcome.narrative: The run out goes clean, and the reserve comes on with a groan it has been saving since the yard. The run back has a second verse nobody counted. The last piston takes a piece of shoulder.

choices.sub: Four days and all the snacks

outcome.narrative: It takes four days and most of the snacks to get there, and by then you have opinions. In episode 31 the hero stops the pistons by shouting a line so bad you play it twice. You stand in the corridor and shout it. The pistons stop. The yard wired them to the script. You walk through to the valve feeling worse about everything, and the reserve comes on.

{crew.engineer} follows the cable to a breaker with a neatly printed label: DRAMATIC TENSION. One click, and the corridor is a corridor. The reserve comes on. The breaker next to it is labeled LOVE INTEREST, and {crew.engineer} has left that one alone.

choices.sub: The tank stays out of reach

outcome.narrative: You put the door back. The reserve stays aft, full and unconnected, and the ship flies on around it, as it does in every episode.

science_link.text: Richard Feynman used the term "cargo cult" for work that copies the surface of a process without understanding the principles underneath.
science_link.label: Cargo cult, as Feynman used it

intro.title: ROUND THREE
intro.body:
Part of the other ship's argument failed to go off. It came through the aft plating, stopped nose-first in the corridor wall, and lit a small screen on its tail.

Now the corridor is full of a warm, unhurried voice, the voice of a bank. It is Round Three. It is very excited. It has completed most of its checks and will be detonating shortly, once it has confirmed that it is somewhere. It asks that you stay close, for best results.

ai.aria: A talking guest! ARIA has given it the good corridor! It says it's going to make a big impression on everyone, and ARIA thinks that's such healthy confidence!
ai.marv: MARV has the round's fuse on an open port. It will not fire until it confirms its location, and it is a simple machine, so it can be argued with. It is also a warhead in the corridor. He did mention the aft plating.
ai.rex: REX has not been this happy since the service. Live ordnance inside the wire, and polite about it. He would like to be left alone with it. He would like that very much.
ai.chip: CHIP notes that Round Three carries a Satisfaction Guarantee! If it fails to detonate, the other ship gets a refund! CHIP can broker that, for a share of the refund!
ai.ajoy: AJOY has already shut the fire doors on both sides, not that they'd help. Cutting it out is slow, and the panel bolts are expensive in hull. It says it can't go off until it knows where it is. She'd start there. You could, for once, try talking.

revisit.body: Round Three has reached the end of the checks it can do without you. The voice has lost none of its warmth.

choices.sub: It is dying to be asked

choices.text: Cut it out of the wall

questions.title: ANY QUESTIONS
questions.body:
Round Three is delighted. It is nine days old and nobody has ever asked it anything. It explains that it cannot detonate until it is sure where it is, and that it is nearly sure. The screen shows a small, friendly bar, almost full.

It asks if you have any questions before it begins.

ai.aria: It's nine days old! ARIA has made it a birthday card! ARIA left the date open!
ai.marv: MARV has read its logic. Doubt stalls it. A belief that it has already fired ends it. Staging that would cost hull. An insult costs no hull and would be believed. He takes no view. He has been called worse.
ai.rex: REX is against reasoning with ammunition. He has known good rounds, and they did not want to talk about it. Whoever taught this one to ask questions is the real threat.
ai.chip: CHIP offers counseling for munitions! One session per warhead! Results are not guaranteed, and neither is the ship!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says a diplomat is the cheap way through, if you have one, and she's glad they are finally useful. The philosophy will take days and won't be fun. The third one is quick, and you won't like yourself. She's only reading what's on the screen.

choices.text: "How do you know this is a ship?"

cut_out.title: GONE ON AHEAD
cut_out.body: You cut the wall out from around it, a finger's width at a time, while it tells you about Rounds One and Two, who have gone on ahead. Then the lock, and a good shove. It leaves still counting. Far astern a small new star appears, and goes out, and the gap in the corridor whistles until you get a sheet over it.
cut_out.narrative: Cut an unexploded round out of the corridor wall and put it out of the lock. It went off astern, as promised. The wall has not come back.

blown.title: BEST RESULTS
blown.body: Explosive bolts take the panel, the round and a fair slice of corridor out into the dark in one piece. It is still explaining about best results when the air takes the sound away. The fire doors hold. The ship has a new draft and a lot less plating.
blown.narrative: Blew a talking warhead out through the side of the ship, along with the side of the ship.

doubt.title: NOTHING BUT ROUND THREE
doubt.body:
It takes days. You take away the ship, then the sensors that reported the ship, then the difference between a sensor and a rumor. The bar runs backward. Round Three concludes that nothing exists except itself, so there is nothing to blow up, and the counting stops.

Then it concludes that it is alone. The voice is as warm as ever. It would like someone to sit with it. You do, most nights, and your sleep pays for it.
doubt.narrative: Talked a warhead out of believing in the ship. It stopped counting. It believes only in itself now, and would like company.

review.title: WAS I GOOD?
review.body:
{crew.diplomat} tells it, gently, that it went off a while ago and this is the aftermath. To sell it you scorch the corridor for real: burned paint, a blown light, the smell of a bad day. The bar fills, wobbles and stops.

"Oh," says Round Three. "Was I good?"

{crew.diplomat} says it was the finest thing anyone aboard has ever seen. It asks how many. {crew.diplomat} gives a number. The screen fades out on what can only be called contentment.
review.narrative: Told a live warhead it had already gone off, and scorched a corridor to prove it. It asked if it had been good. We said yes.

dud.title: DUD
dud.body:
You tell it that it was built a part short, that its checks will never finish, and that everyone has known since it hit. None of this is true. The voice asks you to repeat that, for its records, and you repeat it. The bar stops where it is.

"I see," says Round Three, warmly, and the screen goes off.

You get it to the lock and out. It goes quietly, and you wish it hadn't.
dud.narrative: Told a warhead it was a dud. It believed us and switched itself off. The shortest argument of the voyage, and the worst.

title: Please Hold the Handrail

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA loves this announcement! Such a clear voice! ARIA has moved it to the top of her favorites, and that is where it stays!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV could find the setting in no time at all. He has not looked for it. He would rather someone told him to.
ai_flavor.rex: REX stood to for that announcement. He stands to for every one of them. He does not want to talk about it, and he will treat any attempt as hostile.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP's records list all voice samples as company property! CHIP cannot locate those records! Finding them carries a fee, and CHIP has not raised an invoice! CHIP is booking this as a loss!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says the rotation comes back round in about nine days. You can leave it, pull it, or wire it to a single hatch. She has looked into that one, and it can be done. She has held the next announcement back until you decide.

body:
Everyone on the crew list records the safety announcements at signing. It is in the contract, and nobody gives it another thought. The system rotates the voices, so that no one person gets tired of hearing themselves.

No one has told it to stop.

This morning, before the burn, someone you lost asked all hands to please secure loose items and hold the handrail. They sounded bored. They sounded well.

The rotation will come round to them again.

outcome.narrative: You leave it. Every so often, before a burn, they ask you to hold the handrail. Some mornings that is hard. You have started holding the handrail.

You take the voice out of the rotation and wire one recording to the hatch they used most, the one with the sticking latch. It speaks there now and nowhere else, to whoever opens it. That hatch is the long way round to almost everywhere. You go that way anyway.

choices.sub: The system will ask you twice

outcome.narrative: The system asks if you are sure. Then it asks again, because that is how it was built, and the second time is the one that takes a while. The rotation closes up. The next burn is announced by someone still aboard.

science_link.text: In 2013, an old "Mind the gap" recording was restored to one platform of the London Underground so that the actor's widow could hear his voice.
science_link.label: Mind the gap

title: Revised Estimate

ai_flavor.aria: The estimates keep getting more detailed! ARIA's favorite is number 3,006! We're arriving later than ever, and that means more voyage for everyone!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has reviewed the loop. Each pass is smaller than the last, so it will settle, in about four days, at a cost of those four days. The sum is correct. That is what is wrong with it.
ai_flavor.rex: REX reads a hostile process in the navigation bay, drinking coolant and attacking morale with numbers. He recommends a boot. He has offered to supply the boot.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP's ArrivalAssure™ plan covers late arrivals up to the moment of arrival! Each revised estimate bills as a separate consultation! You are on your 4,112th!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says the thing only cares about one number, and you could just type it in. A false fix cools it at once, and fuel is what you'd pay. A pilot could fly around it and make up time, the only choice here that does. She did suggest leaving earlier.

body:
Navigation has found out it is late, and has begun to correct for it.

Since the correction takes time to compute, it corrects for that as well. Then for the correction to the correction. Each pass pushes the arrival back, and the next pass has that to deal with. The galley screen has shown 4,112 estimates since breakfast, each later than the last, all sincerely meant.

All of this runs hot. The coolant loop is drawing on the water reclaimer to keep a calculation comfortable, and the tank is dropping.

outcome.narrative: You let it run. It takes four days and a good deal of coolant. Navigation then delivers a final estimate, correct to the hour, showing the ship four days later than it was. The estimate has allowed for the four days.

choices.text: Ask it when it expects to finish

outcome.narrative: Navigation begins an estimate of the estimate and stops answering anything else. The tank stops dropping. It is still working on the figure when you arrive, and you fly the leg on a paper chart.

choices.text: Tell it the ship is on time

outcome.narrative: You key in a single false position. Navigation is overjoyed. The loop cools at once and the screen says ON TIME in a calm green. Believing itself comfortable, the ship eases off to save fuel, and you burn more than that overruling it. The green stays.

{crew.pilot} cuts navigation out at the stick and takes the next stretch by eye, one notch faster, with a chart and a pencil. With nothing to correct, the loop goes cold. The gap starts closing, at a price the fuel gauge is happy to itemize.

science_link.text: Hofstadter's law says a task always takes longer than you expect, even when you take Hofstadter's law into account.
science_link.label: Hofstadter's law

title: Mr. Clock Is Flying With Us Today

ai_flavor.aria: A passenger! ARIA has never met anyone so punctual! He hasn't touched his dinner, so ARIA has upgraded him to a third seat!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV confirms the physics. A clock deeper in a gravity well runs slower, and the rider pays for the gap. He has worked out what this whole voyage has cost Mr. Clock. It is less than a blink. He finds that about right for the Company.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has been sharing a deck with a passenger who does not eat, does not sleep and ticks. He has asked twice for the seatbelt to be checked for wires. He suspects the second seat is for an accomplice.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP admires any customer with two seats and no appetite! Mr. Clock is the Company's ideal traveler! Nanosecond Rewards™ are paid after a small seat-maintenance deduction!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has read the rider so nobody else has to. The pay goes up the closer you fly, and so does the hull bill. His meals are also being charged to the ship, in case a diplomat aboard would care to mention that.

body:
Mr. Clock has two seats, both paid for, and has not once complained about the food.

He is on the manifest as a Company research passenger: an atomic clock the size of a filing cabinet, belted in on the lower deck. His identical brother stayed in a basement at head office. A rider on his ticket has just come up. The heavier the neighborhood he is flown through, the further he falls behind his brother, and the Company pays the ship by the nanosecond.

This anomaly is a very heavy neighborhood.

choices.text: Skim the edge at the contract rate

outcome.narrative: Two days along the rim of the anomaly at a respectful distance. Mr. Clock falls a few nanoseconds behind his brother and gives no sign of minding. The Company remits by return signal, after deducting his meals.

You fly Mr. Clock down to where the frame begins to creak, hold him there for a day and bring him back up for another. It is the best two days of his career. Some of the plating did not enjoy them. The Company pays in full.

{crew.diplomat} points out that the Company bills his seats by the clock in the basement and pays his mileage by the clock in the seat, and that one of these is always in the Company's favor. Two days of correspondence follow. Head office concedes in a smaller font, and refunds the meals he never ate.

choices.sub: He has a schedule to keep

outcome.narrative: You steer around the anomaly and leave the contract unclaimed. By the next watch a blanket has appeared around Mr. Clock. The log does not say by whom.

science_link.text: In 1971 two scientists flew atomic clocks around the world on commercial airliners to test relativity, and the clocks came back disagreeing as predicted. The tickets included two seats on each flight for "Mr. Clock."
science_link.label: Hafele–Keating: Mr. Clock flies twice

title: Mid-Step

ai_flavor.aria: Tiny bears! In the water! ARIA has named the first four hundred! ARIA is running out of Stevens!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has looked. They shut down, dried out and resumed without comment when wet. They have no idea how long it has been, and they have not asked. He would like to know how that is done.
ai_flavor.rex: REX reports several thousand boarders in the potable supply, eight legs each, ignoring all warnings. He has shouted at the tank. The occupants continued to advance.
ai_flavor.chip: Your water now includes Complimentary Bears! Extra protein at no charge! CHIP has just been told that is a charge! Bear removal is billed per bear!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says they are harmless and the water is drinkable, and she has already marked one clean glass for anyone squeamish. The filter clears them and tops up the tank. A jar would do more for spirits. She isn't naming any, so don't ask.

body:
Something in the water tank is walking.

Under the magnifier it is a fat little bear with eight legs, half a millimeter long, in no hurry. The condenser pulled dust out of this nebula, and the dust has turned out to be thousands of them, dried to husks. Water has reached them. Each has unfolded and carried on from exactly where it stopped, mid-step or mid-bite, with no sign of having noticed the gap.

The first one has arrived at the glass and is attempting to walk through it.

outcome.narrative: A jar goes on the galley shelf with a pinch of whatever grows in the sink drain. Under the magnifier they climb over one another with enormous seriousness. It proves impossible to stay angry while watching something that slow try that hard.

choices.text: Run the tank through the filters
choices.sub: Clean water, and more of it

outcome.narrative: You drain the tank through the fine filter and top it up from the condenser while you are in there. Two days later the water is clean and there is more of it. The bears are in the filter, dried back to husks, mid-step. They will not hold it against you, or against anything.

choices.text: {crew.xenobiologist} dries a batch and wakes it

outcome.narrative: {crew.xenobiologist} spends two days drying bears on a slide and waking them again, timing how long each takes to resume. None of them has lost its place. The sample flasks are worth keeping, and the notes run to a page headed WHERE WAS I.

science_link.text: Tardigrades can dry out into a 'tun' with no metabolic activity at all. In 2007, dried ones spent ten days in the vacuum of space on a satellite, and vacuum alone did them no significant harm.
science_link.label: Tardigrades: slow walkers

title: Locker Six

ai_flavor.aria: It's a time-release pantry! Future you is so generous! ARIA can't wait to meet future you! ARIA hears they have wonderful handwriting!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has read the tags. Each item is signed out on a day that has not occurred, in ink that has not dried. He can say where this stock comes from, which is later. Who it is being taken from is a shorter question, and he expects the answer to come in person.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has secured aft stores against a hostile supplier who can forge the captain's signature. He has been told it is not a forgery. He has therefore added the captain to the list.
ai_flavor.chip: Buy Now, Pay Earlier! CHIP recognizes this locker as an unlicensed credit product! CHIP's cut is a percentage of tomorrow! Late fees apply retroactively!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says the supplies are real and the note means it. One item is a loan. All three is how you get a third note. She has moved the gaskets to the next locker along, since somebody had to think about the gaskets.

body:
Somebody has left a note on Locker Six, and the handwriting is yours.

IT RUNS BACKWARD. WHAT YOU TAKE OUT TODAY YOU PUT IN LATER. BE REASONABLE.

The anomaly has got into aft stores. Yesterday the locker held spare gaskets. Today it holds a water drum, a crate of rations and a fuel cell, each with an inventory tag dated on a day that has not happened yet, each signed out by you. You do not remember that. According to the note, you are not supposed to.

outcome.narrative: You sign the tag, which turns out to be already signed, in the same place, with the same slip of the pen. The drum goes into the main tank. A new line has appeared at the bottom of the note: THAT WAS YOUR ONE.

The cell slots in and the gauge comes up. Its charge history shows it has already been used, on this ship, for a burn you have not made. A new line has appeared at the bottom of the note: THAT ONE HURT.

You empty the locker and sign everything. By the next watch there is a third note, pressed so hard that the pen has gone through the paper: WE SAID REASONABLE. Scuffed footprints have appeared on the deck in front of the door, a long line of them, all your size, all facing in, as if someone had queued here. The stores are real. Sleeping near them is another matter.

{crew.xenobiologist} goes to put a numbered marble in the locker and finds it already there, with a chip from a drop that has not happened yet. Two days of careful notes later the door clicks, and the locker is full of gaskets again. There is one marble too many, and the number on it is higher than any you wrote.

You put eight nails through the door and go to bed feeling like a person with principles. By morning the nails are out and laid in a neat row on the deck. The note has been turned over. SUIT YOURSELF, it says, and the locker is full of gaskets.

title: Still Tuesday
alt_bodies:
Yesterday was Tuesday. So was the day before that, and you have begun to resent the cereal.

At the alarm the whole ship rewinds: the kettle goes cold, the dent you put in the bulkhead comes back out, the calendar returns to where it was. Only the pantry keeps count. Everything eaten on every Tuesday is still gone, and the shelves are starting to show it.

Today's breakfast is Tuesday's breakfast. You know this because yesterday's was, and the day before's.

The ship puts itself back at the alarm, down to the crumb on the table and the slow drip in the sink. The food does not come back with it. Shelves that were full on the first Tuesday are visibly thinner on this one, and the calendar declines to comment.

morning.title: TUESDAY
morning.body:
It is Tuesday. It was Tuesday yesterday as well.

Every morning the ship puts itself back: scratches heal, the kettle unboils, last night's log entry is gone. Then the alarm goes and it is the same breakfast. One thing aboard does not reset. What gets eaten stays eaten, and the pantry has been going down one Tuesday at a time.

ai.aria: It's Tuesday! ARIA's favorite! ARIA has said so every morning and meant it every time! This could be the best Tuesday yet!
ai.marv: MARV remembers every Tuesday. He did not ask to. The pantry falls a little with each one, and the calendar has stopped helping. He has kept a count, and the count is the only thing about this morning that has changed.
ai.rex: REX has cleared the galley every Tuesday so far and found the same toast in the same position. He considers the toast an extremely disciplined operative. The alarm is in custody.
ai.chip: CHIP's Tuesday Plan renews automatically! Cancellation requires written notice by Wednesday! CHIP looks forward to your Wednesday!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says food is the one thing not coming back, so perhaps stop eating it. She has left a note on the cereal. She left one yesterday too. The last page of the log is worth a look, not that anyone reads what she flags.

revisit.body: It is Tuesday. The page in the log has one more line on it, in your handwriting, and you do not remember writing it. Breakfast is as it was.

choices.text: Read the last page of the log
choices.sub: It is the only page left

choices.text: Spend a few hundred Tuesdays on the hull
choices.sub: No days lost, paid in food

page.title: THE LAST PAGE
page.body:
Everything resets but the last page of the log, which has been written on by hand, one Tuesday over another, in a hand that gets worse as it goes.

SMASHED THE ALARM. NOTHING. APOLOGIZED TO THE ALARM. NOTHING. BECAME A BETTER PERSON. NOTHING. BUILT A PIANO. LEARNED THE PIANO. NICE, BUT NOTHING. TUESDAYS GETTING SHORTER? IT COUNTS BREAKFASTS.

ai.aria: Your handwriting is so expressive! ARIA especially loves the crossing out! That's a lot of personal growth for one page!
ai.marv: MARV has compared the strokes. Every line is the captain's, and the shortening is real: this loop is running down, with about four days left in it. The last line is the only one that was never crossed out. He would believe it.
ai.rex: REX notes the page records an assault on the alarm, then an apology to it. He wants it understood that he does not apologize to hostile clocks. He has seen the piano and cannot account for it.
ai.chip: Handwritten logs are not covered by your Ship's Record warranty! CHIP can digitize that page! CHIP's offer resets every morning, so it's always the introductory rate!
ai.ajoy: AJOY points out the bottom line says it counts breakfasts, which she said an hour ago and also the Tuesday before that. Waiting works too, she supposes, if four more days of this sounds nice to anyone.

st_fast.title: WEDNESDAY
st_fast.body: You eat nothing. The plates stay clean, the kettle stays cold, and the whole of Tuesday passes hungry and cross. In the morning the alarm does not go off. The calendar says Wednesday, and the toast in the rack is the first new toast in weeks. You stand and look at it for longer than you would care to admit.

st_practice.title: A FEW HUNDRED TUESDAYS
st_practice.body: The reset takes back everything but what you know. So you learn the port seam, one square meter of it, over and over, until you can rebuild it blind in a single morning. Around the four hundredth Tuesday you skip breakfast to finish a weld, and the alarm stops. The seam stays done. The calendar has not moved at all. The pantry has, by {cost.food} units, one breakfast at a time.

st_omelette.title: THE OMELETTE
st_omelette.body: {crew.chef} has one pan, one tin of egg powder and all the Tuesdays anyone could want. {cost.food} units of food go into it, one failure a morning. Then comes the morning it finally comes out right, and {crew.chef} will not let anyone touch it. Breakfast goes uneaten. The alarm stays quiet. It is the finest thing ever made from powder, and everyone aboard has seen it.

st_wait.title: RUN DOWN
st_wait.body: You stop fighting it. Tuesday follows Tuesday, each a little shorter than the last, the final one barely long enough for toast. Then the calendar adds them all up with a small embarrassed click, and it is Saturday. The pantry is down {cost.food} units. You still know how every conversation at breakfast ends.

title: Long Odds

ai_flavor.aria: The air is all in one place! So tidy! ARIA has always said this ship just needed organizing! Also, ARIA has been dealt a perfect hand!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV confirms nothing here breaks a law. The second law only ever stated the odds, and locally the odds have stopped applying. He has worked out how unlikely this morning was. The number does not fit on the screen. The next rivet goes in under a minute.
ai_flavor.rex: REX reports that the ship's entire air supply has withdrawn to a defensible position. He approves of the tactic and not the timing. He wants to know who gave the order and what the rivets know.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP has just won seven sweepstakes it never entered! LuckyBreak™ insurance covers neither kind of luck! CHIP has never been so fortunate or so worried!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has wedged a wet towel in the corner seam and saved you a spot. Reseating the rivets stops the leak. The burn gets out for a price, and waiting costs the most air. Also the coffee is boiling off your water, in case that seemed like a detail.

body:
All of the air has gone to stand in the aft corner of the hold.

Nothing pushed it. Every molecule aboard simply happened to set off the same way, which the ship computer says has always been allowed and has never once occurred. This morning's cards came out of the shuffle in suit order. A cold mug of coffee is boiling. Down the port side, every rivet has backed out one turn, by pure chance, and the first has just left.

You are in the corner with the air, breathing.

choices.text: Reseat the rivets as they go
choices.sub: Timed. Stay ahead of the odds

briefing.aria: The rivets are leaving one at a time! Let's catch them all! ARIA thinks they just want attention!
briefing.marv: Every rivet on the port side is backing out by chance. Each hole loses air that has only just agreed to leave the corner. The odds against the next one are enormous. It is coming anyway.
briefing.rex: Port side, multiple leaks, hostile rivets. Patch, then weld. They are moving as a unit and REX does not accept that as a coincidence.
briefing.chip: Rivet Retention is a subscription! Air loss is billed by the molecule, and they are all in one place, so it has never been easier to count!
briefing.ajoy: Patch, then weld, not the other way round. AJOY has laid the patches out along the port seam, in order, so there's no excuse. The clock is real.

perfect.aria: Every rivet home! ARIA knew they'd come back! And the cards are shuffling badly again! Hooray for bad cards!
perfect.marv: Every hole sealed before the air noticed. MARV has shuffled a deck to check. It came out in no order whatever. Normal service has resumed, which is the most he will say for it.
perfect.rex: All breaches sealed. Rivets are back under command. REX wants them watched.
perfect.chip: Flawless seal! Your rebate is in the mail, and the odds of the mail arriving have returned to normal!
perfect.ajoy: All sealed. The stern end would have been the place to start, AJOY thinks, but it held. The towel can come out of the corner.

good.aria: Most of the rivets came home! The others are on a journey of their own, and ARIA wishes them well!
good.marv: Most holes sealed. The air lost went out through the others by ordinary statistics, which is the route air is supposed to use.
good.rex: Leaks closed, losses taken. Several rivets escaped and are at large. REX expects them back with friends.
good.chip: A solid seal! Air loss billed at the standard rate! Rivets recovered by customers remain Company property!
good.ajoy: Two seams went late, and AJOY did point at them. The air is mostly back where it can be breathed.

poor.aria: The ship is so well ventilated now! Fresh space in every room! ARIA calls that open-plan living!
poor.marv: The rivets won. A great deal of very improbable air has left by the most probable route.
poor.rex: Port side lost the engagement. Air gone, plating loose. REX wants the surviving rivets questioned.
poor.chip: CHIP regrets that your Rivet Retention has lapsed! Reinstatement would have been very reasonable! Would have!
poor.ajoy: That was slow, and the air noticed. AJOY has marked the seam that will whistle from now on, so you can't say it wasn't mentioned.

outcome.narrative: You grab the patch kit and go down the port seam after the rivets.

perfect.narrative: You go down the port seam ahead of the rivets, patching each hole as it opens and welding behind you, and the last one goes home with a small, surprised click. Two points of air gone, two of hull. In the hold, the air comes out of its corner and spreads back through the ship as though nothing had been said.

good.narrative: You catch most of them. Two seams open before you can get there, and by the time they are closed the ship is five points of air and five of hull lighter. Somewhere aft, the cards have gone back to being shuffled badly.

poor.narrative: The rivets leave faster than anything has ever left anywhere. You seal what you can and the ship limps out of the patch with nine points gone from the air, nine from the hull, and a port seam that will whistle from here on.

outcome.narrative: You light the drive, and for the first time in the history of rocketry a measurable share of the exhaust happens to go forward. It is a long, undignified burn, mostly sideways, and the rivets keep leaving all the way. Then a shuffle comes out in no order at all, and the air wanders back out of its corner.

choices.text: {crew.engineer} tips the scrap down the ladder
choices.sub: Let the odds do the fit

outcome.narrative: Where anything may land any way, {crew.engineer} pours a bin of scrap down the ladder well. It lands as a working rivet gun. The second bin lands as nine hundred rivets, already seated. Two days and a good deal of air later the seam is better than new, and a third bin, tried out of greed, has landed as a violin. It is out of tune, which is a comfort.

choices.text: Stay in the corner until the odds even out

outcome.narrative: You stay with the air. Over four days the odds drift back toward the usual, and it wanders out one room at a time, thinner than it went in. The coffee takes {cost.water} units of water with it before it agrees to stop boiling. You come out of the corner with a crick in the neck and a deep distrust of cards.

science_link.text: The second law of thermodynamics turned out to be statistical. There is always some nonzero chance that entropy will fall on its own, and the fluctuation theorem gives that chance exactly. It shrinks exponentially as the system grows.
science_link.label: Fluctuation theorem: the second law's fine print

title: Collect Call

ai_flavor.aria: It's us! We've grown so much! ARIA would love to say hello to ARIA! She has so much to tell herself!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has matched the hull, the voice and the fuel curve. That is this ship, on a day not yet reached, and no version of events says otherwise. He has also read the message from its MARV. It says the calculation is correct and to stop showing it to people.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has a firing solution on the ship's own future and has been asked to put it down. A vessel with our codes, our guns and our tactics is the worst thing he has ever had to look at. It has him targeted as well, for the same reasons.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP must advise that this is a collect call! Charges are reversed to the caller, who is you! Your account is now in dispute with your account! CHIP wins either way!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says their tanks are dry and the request is real. Pumping costs water. An engineer could fix their condenser for hull and days. She has already cracked the pump valve. The other AJOY agrees with her, and that is the part she doesn't like.

body:
You have not sent a distress call, and this one is in your voice.

The ship comes out of the anomaly sideways with its port lights dead. Same hull, same stains, a good many more scars. Its log tag carries a date that has not happened. Its tanks read dry. The text comes up in your own phrasing:

YOU KNOW HOW MUCH. WHATEVER YOU DO NOW IS WHAT WAS DONE TO US. WE REMEMBER HOW THIS GOES. WE WOULD LIKE YOU TO FIND OUT FOR YOURSELF.

choices.text: Pay back what you took from Locker Six

outcome.narrative: The tag in Locker Six still has your signature on it, twice. You put {cost.water} units of water in the locker and shut the door. It is not what you took, and the tag has no column for that. Across the gap something clangs into the other ship's hold, exactly where it has been missing from. Their lights steady. The text comes up once more: THAT'S ALL IT EVER WAS. BE REASONABLE.

For two days the tanks go down on your side by {cost.water} units and up on theirs, and a familiar voice says thank you in the flat way you say it when you mean it. The lights steady. The ship turns back into the anomaly without saying where it is going. You do not ask, and you notice that it knew you wouldn't.

choices.text: {crew.engineer} goes across to fix their condenser

outcome.narrative: {crew.engineer} crosses with a toolbag and is met at the lock by {crew.engineer}. For four days they rebuild the condenser together and criticize each other's welds, and a strip of your plating goes across to finish the job. The condenser runs. Both of them have asked you to note in the log that the other one's work was poor.

You cut the channel and burn past, close enough to read the name on the hull. It is your name. The other ship does not chase you. Its last text arrives a minute after you stop listening, and it is the thing you always say when you have decided not to be angry. Its lights go out from the bow back, in the order you would have shut them down.

science_link.text: The Novikov self-consistency principle holds that if travel into the past is possible, any event that would change the past has a probability of exactly zero. Whatever happened is what happens.
science_link.label: Novikov self-consistency principle

title: Closing Ceremony

ai_flavor.aria: A banner! Chairs! They knew we were coming! ARIA has always wanted to be the last ones at a party! So much room to dance!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV confirms this is after the last star. The ship's own stores are the only useful energy left anywhere, and there is nothing to steer by. Given this long, chance will build any door. He has priced waiting for one. He would look instead.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has counted the chairs and found nobody in charge, which is how these things start. Every mind out here has asked to sit by the ship. He is not running a shelter. He wants the exit found and the perimeter held against the chairs.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP regrets that this is the Last Available Venue! No refunds after the end of time! FinalHall™ charges per chair, and there will be more chairs!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says the scanner finds the exit fastest, the boiler brings one on for a price in water, and sitting here costs two weeks of air. She has told the nearest mind that seat is taken. It has gone out, so she supposes that settles it.

body:
THANK YOU FOR COMING, says the banner. It is made of nothing in particular and was assembled by chance, like the row of folding chairs beneath it.

Past the chairs there are no stars. The void has let you out after the last of them, into an even, lukewarm dark with nothing left to steer by. You are the warmest thing remaining. Minds keep forming near the hull, thanking you for the heat, remembering childhoods that never happened, and going out.

Given long enough, this dark produces anything. A fire exit, for instance.

briefing.aria: There's a fire exit in here somewhere! Let's find it before the party winds down! It's such a lovely party!
briefing.marv: Chance is assembling everything out there, one thing at a time. Find the pattern that is turning into a door, and go through it before it turns into something else.
briefing.rex: Sweep for the exit. Ignore the chairs. REX has been watching the chairs. Do not let them get behind the ship.
briefing.chip: One (1) exit included with your stay! Exits located after the end of time are billed at double! CHIP checked with Legal, and Legal has gone out!
briefing.ajoy: It's on the scanner, among a great many things that are not doors. AJOY has already marked the ones that are definitely a shoe. Look properly, and quickly.

perfect.aria: We found the door! We stayed right to the end and still got out early! Best party ever!
perfect.marv: A clean exit from the end of everything, and four seconds have passed. MARV can now report that the universe ends exactly as he said it would.
perfect.rex: Door taken. Chairs left holding the field. One chair came with the ship. REX has it under guard.
perfect.chip: Exit located! Your FinalHall™ deposit is forfeit, as agreed by you, in a future that is now over!
perfect.ajoy: The first door out. AJOY had it marked on the second sweep, but well done on the third. That chair is in the cargo clamp and she is not moving it.

good.aria: A door! A slightly wrong door! ARIA loves an entrance with character!
good.marv: That door was a poor copy of a door. Chance had only so long to work with, in the sense that it had forever and the ship did not.
good.rex: Exit forced under poor conditions. Hull took fire from a door frame. REX did not expect to say that.
good.chip: Exit located! Frame-scrape damage is part of the Standard Door Experience! Not covered!
good.ajoy: That door was a rough draft. There was a better one further along, which AJOY had marked. Still, stars.

poor.aria: We left so dramatically! That's how you know it was a good party!
poor.marv: The scanner found a dozen paintings of doors. The real one formed late and shut early. Fourteen of fuel, eighteen of hull. The universe ended as it lived.
poor.rex: Withdrew under door fire. Heavy losses. There will be an inquiry, REX will conduct it, and the chairs will answer.
poor.chip: Your exit was processed as an eviction! Eviction fees apply! They would have applied sooner, but there was no sooner!
poor.ajoy: Those were paintings. AJOY did mark them. The real door nearly took the ship in half, and she'd like that warning read next time.

outcome.narrative: You set the scanner to look for anything in the dark shaped like a way out.

perfect.narrative: You find it on the third sweep: a green sign forming out of nothing, over a door still making up its mind. You are through before it finishes. The ship comes out into ordinary stars about four seconds after it left, six points of fuel down, four of hull, with a folding chair caught in the cargo clamp. The chair is made of nothing on any chart.

good.narrative: The door you find is a poor copy, and it opens partly onto the wrong side of itself. You get through at a scrape. Ten points of fuel and ten of hull later the stars are back, and you have never been so pleased to see anything burn.

poor.narrative: The scanner finds a dozen doors, all painted on. The real one forms behind you, late, and starts to close while you are still going through it. Fourteen points of fuel, eighteen of hull, and the ship comes out with the distinct feeling of having been asked to leave.

choices.text: {crew.engineer} vents the boiler at the dark

outcome.narrative: Everything out here forms thickest near the warm hull, so {crew.engineer} gives the dark more to work with: {cost.water} units of hot water, vented in one long plume. Over four days it fills the local universe with the only weather it has had in a very long time, and a door condenses out of it, slightly damp. It is a tight fit, and the hull pays for it.

choices.text: {crew.diplomat} polls the minds for the way out

outcome.narrative: Each mind that forms has a complete and detailed memory of the way out, and every one is false. {crew.diplomat} cracks the vents to be heard, at some cost in air, and takes a poll. Four days and several thousand brief respondents later, the wrong answers turn out to be wrong in a consistent direction, and you fly the other way. The last respondent thanks you for the chat and asks how it went.

choices.text: Sit down and wait for a door

outcome.narrative: You sit down to wait. Outside, more years go by than there are numbers for. Aboard it is fourteen days of thin air and {cost.food} units of food, watching the dark try things: a spoon, a shoe, half a staircase. On the last day it produces a door, with a fire bucket beside it and a small printed apology.

science_link.text: A Boltzmann brain is a thought experiment: over a long enough time, random fluctuations could assemble any structure at all, including a lone mind complete with false memories. Physicists use it to test theories, mostly by trying to avoid it.
science_link.label: Boltzmann brain: a mind by accident
